( r"rst Revision)
0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 15 October 1986, after the draft finalized by the Chemical Methods of Test Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council., 0.2 This standard was first published in 1966 and has been revised to align it with IS0 105-E13-1978 `Textiles -Test for colour fastness to acidfelting : Severe', issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ). Changes have been made in the preparation of composite specimen and sampling. It differs from IS0 standard in respect of sampling of textile material.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes a method for determination of colour fastness of textile materials of all kinds and in all forms to the action of acids as used under severe conditions in the acid felting process. 2. PRINCIPLE 2.1 A specimen of the textile in contact with adjacent fabrics is treated with solutions of acetic acid and/or sulphuric acid, rinsed and dried. The change in colour of the specimen and the staining of Lhe adjacent fabrics is assessed with slandard grey scales. 3. SAMPLING 3.1 Sample to determine conformity of a lot to a specification selected so as to be representative of the lot. 3 shall be

IS:3425-1986 3.2 Sample drawn in compliance with the material specification or as agreed to between the buyer and the seller to evaluate the colour fastness of the textile material in the lot to acid-felting : severe, shall be held to be representative of the lot. 4. APPARATUS 4.1 A suitable an appropriate open contzin-r and a glass rod flattened mechanical device ( see Note ). it one end, or

NOTE - Launderomctcr of American Association of Textile Chemists and Colotrrists or W:!~,hahcel s~~,~-~sorcd by the Society of Dyers and Colourists, may be used. Other simil:lr mc ch.~nic;~l device may also be used for the tests provided the results obtained arc itlztitit,;l to those obtained with apparatus described in 4.1.

4.2

Two adjacent fabrics, each measuring 10 X 4 cm, one piece made of wool and the other also made of wool or of another fibre to be assessed for slaining, as desired ( .scc Appendix A ). in colour and staining ( see

4.3 Grey scales for aszcssing change IS : 768-1982* and JS : 769-19S2f ). 5. REAGENTS

5.1 Quality of Reagents --- Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals s!:all be employed in tests and distilled water ( SLYIS : 1070-19771) shall be used where the USCof v,atcr as rengcnt is intended.

containing

OF COMPOSITE

6.1 If the textile to be tested is fabric, draw at least three test specimens 10 X 4,cm from the test sample ( SW 3.2 ). Place a test specimen between the two adjacent fabrics ( see 4.2 ) and sew along all four sides to f&m a composite specimen. Similarly, treat other test specimen to form composite specimens.
*Method for evaluating change in eolour (first rrvision ). tMethod for evaluating staining (first revisipn ). $Specification for water for general laboratory use ( second revision ).

IS : 3425- 1986 6.2 If the textile to be tested is yarn, knit or weave the test sample (see3.2) into a fabric and treat as in 6.1, or form a layer of parallel lengths of yarn between the two adjacent fabrics ( see 4.2 ), the amount of yarn taken being approximately equal to half the combined mass of the adjacent fabrics. Sew along all four sides to hold the yarn in place and to Prepare at least three such composite form a composite specimen. specimens. 6.3 If the textile to be tested is loose fibre, comb and compress, from the test sample, an amount approximately equal to half the combined mass of the adjacent fabrics ( SW 4.2 ) into a sheet 10 X 4 cm. Place the sheet between the two adjacent fabrics and sew along all four sides to hold the fibres in place and to form a composite specimen. Prepare at least three such composite specimens. 7. PROCEDURE 7.1 Take thk requisite amount of sulphuric and/or acetic acid solution ( see Note 1 ) in a container to give a liquor to material ratio of 40 : 1. Raise the temperature of the solution to 90 f 2�C. Immerse one composite specimen in the solution for 30 minutes at 90 f 2�C. NOTE 1 -The tests with sulphuric acid and. acetic acid are carried out as separate tests or with only one of the two reagents ( see 5.2 and 5.3 ) as required.
NOTE 2 - The mechanical milling those of hand milling. may be used. device set `to give results, identical with

NOTE 3 -During milling by hand, move the composite specimen continuously with the glass rod while it is in the milling bath and press it with the rod every two minutes, without removing from the bath.

7.2 Remove the ,specimen, rinse it for 10 minutes in cold running water and drain it. Remove the stitching along all sides except one of the. shorter sides. Open out the composite specimen and dry it by hanging in air at a temperature not exceeding 6O"C, with the three parts in contact only at the remaining line of stitching. 7.3 Evaluate the change in colour of the treated test specimen by the method prescribed in IS : 768-1982* and the degree of staining of the two adjacent fabrics by the method prescribed in IS : 769-1982t.
NOTE 1 - Treated test piece after drying and should have evaluation. and Ihe two adjacent fabrics should have cooled regained their normal moisttire content before

NOTE 2 -In cases of doubt in the colour fastness rating as assessed by an observer, the assessment may be made by three observers and the overall average rating may be reported accordingly. *Method tMethod for evaluating for evaluating change in colour (first revision ). staining (first revision ).

5

IS : 3425 - 1986

7.4 Repeat the test with the remaining composite specimens.
8. REPORT 8.1 Report individually (a) the numerical rating for change in colour of the test specimen and (b) the numerical ratings for staining of the two adjacent fabrics used in the preparation of composite specimen.
